cards.q: What is the accumulation administration fee?
cards.a: The lesser of $96 or 2% of the balance a year: at most $8 a month, at month end. Under $4,800 at month end: one month of the 2% fee.
cards.detail: Balanced investment fee 0.39% plus 0.06% transaction costs. On $50,000: $321 a year.

sources.quote: If at the end of the month your account balance is less than $4,800 (including investment returns, where applied) you'll be charged one month's worth of the 2% annual fee.
be charged fees and costs of $321 for the superannuation product.

cards.q: Is there a fee cap for small balances?
cards.a: Yes. Under $6,000 at the end of UniSuper's income year, certain admin and investment fees are capped at 3% of the balance; any excess is refunded.

sources.quote: If your account balance is less than $6,000 at the end of UniSuper's income year, certain fees and costs charged to you in relation to administration and investment are capped at 3% of the account balance.

cards.q: Can fees change?
cards.a: Yes, generally reviewed each year; 30 days' written notice before a new or increased direct fee. Fees aren't negotiable by members.

sources.quote: We'll give you 30 days' written notice before a new or increased fee that we charge directly takes effect.
UniSuper's fees are set at a competitive level that is consistent with effective management and are not negotiable by members.

cards.q: Can financial adviser fees come from the account?
cards.a: Yes, an agreed advice fee can be paid from the account. It's stated in the Statement of Advice.

sources.quote: Those fees will be stated in a Statement of Advice that is provided to you.

cards.q: When does an investment switch take effect?
cards.a: Online before 2pm on a Melbourne business day: processed two Melbourne business days later. Up to three business days overall. Online switches count as received on Submit; paper ones when entered into the system.
cards.detail: No switching fee. An online switch can be replaced before 2pm the same day.

sources.quote: Requests received before 2pm on a Melbourne business day are processed two Melbourne business days later.
you can replace it with a new online switch before 2pm that same day and the first switch won't get processed

cards.q: Where is super invested if the member hasn't chosen?
cards.a: Balanced (MySuper). Members can set a future contributions strategy and a rollover strategy, and switch existing balances.

sources.quote: we'll automatically invest any contributions and transfers to your account in our default investment option, Balanced (MySuper).

cards.q: How are investment returns applied?
cards.a: Daily interim crediting rates, then a final rate each quarter. Returns are applied as a transaction after 30 June and 31 December, and on a switch or withdrawal.

sources.quote: following 30 June and 31 December each year when the final crediting rates are declared

cards.q: Are there limits on rolling super out?
cards.a: Up to eight transfers in any 12 months. A partial transfer must leave at least $6,000, and is taken pro-rata across options.

sources.quote: You may request a transfer up to eight times in each 12-month period.
If you're not transferring the entire amount out of your UniSuper account then you must leave at least $6,000 in your account.

cards.q: When is an inactive account sent to the ATO?
cards.a: Inactive for 16 months with a balance under $6,000 (DBD excluded). The ATO tries to combine it with another active account.

sources.quote: If your account has been identified as inactive for a period of 16 months and has a balance of less than $6,000, we're required to send it to the ATO

cards.q: When is a member treated as lost?
cards.a: Broadly: no address ever held, or mail returned, and no contact, online access, contribution or rollover in the last 12 months. Lost members under $6,000 go to the ATO.

sources.quote: you have not electronically accessed details about your superannuation account within the last 12 months

cards.q: When does super become unclaimed money?
cards.a: At eligibility age with no contributions for two years and no contact for five years; or a former temporary resident after six months and an ATO notice. The member then claims from the ATO.

sources.quote: UniSuper hasn't had contact with you in the last five years

cards.q: What if a member has two UniSuper accounts?
cards.a: We check every year and merge them where it's in the member's best interests, and tell them.

sources.quote: Super legislation requires us to check annually whether members have multiple super accounts with us.

cards.q: Who can open a Personal Account?
aliases: who can open a personal account
cards.a: Anyone aged 15+, living in Australia, with a personal email. Apply online at unisuper.com.au/join. Starting with an eligible employer, the employer sets up an account instead.

sources.quote: To be eligible to open a Personal Account with UniSuper, you must:
have a valid personal email address.

cards.q: How does an Accumulation 1 account get opened?
cards.a: The eligible employer opens it; no application needed. Defaults: Balanced investment, and default insurance if eligible.

sources.quote: Your employer is able to open an account on your behalf, so there's no need to complete an application.

cards.q: What happens to Accumulation 2 when a member leaves their eligible employer?
cards.a: They're moved to Accumulation 1, and can't rejoin Accumulation 2.

sources.quote: Accumulation 2 members will be automatically transferred to Accumulation 1 if they're no longer employed by an eligible employer.
Once a member has exited Accumulation 2 they cannot re-join this product.

cards.q: What happens to DBD when a member changes jobs?
cards.a: Within higher education and still eligible: stays in DBD. Outside the sector: needs to defer membership to stay in DBD.

sources.quote: If you change to a job outside the sector, you will need to defer your membership to remain a DBD member.

cards.q: Will a member be compensated for an error?
cards.a: For material errors caused by UniSuper, generally where the error is 0.30% of the account or more. On closed accounts, under $20 (unit pricing) or $5 (other) isn't usually paid.

sources.quote: UniSuper will generally use a materiality threshold of 0.30% of the account when compared to the amount of the error

cards.q: How does a member get confirmation of a transaction?
cards.a: Call and quote the member number, write to Level 1, 385 Bourke Street, Melbourne, or view and download it online.

sources.quote: To obtain confirmation of a transaction or change, call and quote your member number.

cards.q: How long do complaints take?
cards.a: Super complaints 45 days; advice complaints 30 days; death benefit objections 90 days after the 28-day objection window. If unresolved, AFCA on 1800 931 678.

sources.quote: 45 days for super complaints
90 days for objections to death benefit distributions (starting after the 28-day deadline to submit your objection).

cards.q: Where do members get financial advice?
cards.a: UniSuper Advice: 1800 823 842 or advice@unisuper.com.au.

sources.quote: Email advice@unisuper.com.au or call UniSuper Advice on 1800 823 842.

cards.q: Can super be split on separation?
cards.a: Yes, by agreement or court order. See the Super and family law fact sheet, or request information with the Family law information request form.

sources.quote: can be split between the parties by agreement or court order.
